title: SPA/837/2017 of New Arban Agro Multi State Cooperative Society Ltd Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Special Appeal No. 837 of 2017
New Arban Agro Multi State Co-operative Society Ltd.
 .......... Appellant

Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others .......... Respondents
Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate for the appellant.
Ms. Puja Banga, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/respondents.
Dated : 25th October, 2017

Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.

K.M. Joseph, C.J. (Oral)
 Appellant is the writ petitioner. The reliefs sought in the
writ petition are as follows:
"i) issue a writ, order in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents to decide the
representations of the petitioner dated 11/1/16 and
16/1/16 as directed by this Hon'ble Court vide order
dated 12/7/2016 passed in Writ Petition (M/S) No.
1904/2016 New Arban Agro Multi State Co-operative
Society Ltd. Vs. State of Uttarakhand and others.
ii) issue a writ, order in the nature of mandamus
commanding the respondents Nos. 3, 4, 5, 6 & 7 to
allot 200 acres land to the petitioner society within
Tehsil Vikas Nagar, District Dehradun or any other
place in Uttarakhand without any fee."

2. As far as the first relief is concerned, the learned Single
Judge found that if the writ petitioner was aggrieved by non-compliance of the direction given in the earlier writ petition, the
remedy lies in filing contempt petition. As far as the second relief

2
is concerned, the learned Single Judge has declined the said
relief.

3. Heard Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel on behalf of the
appellant/writ petitioner and Ms. Puja Banga, learned Brief
Holder on behalf of the State/respondents.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that
almost 5,272 Hectares of land is lying vacant in Tehsil
Vikasnagar, in response to a query under the Right to
Information Act. The case of the appellant appears to be that
Agriculture Department has taken the view that it is a matter, in
which the decision is to be taken by the Revenue Department.
The stand of the Revenue Department is that there is no vacant
land, which is disproved by the answer given to the query under
the Right to Information Act. Learned counsel for the appellant
further relies on Article 43B of the Constitution of India, which
was inserted w.e.f. 15.02.2012 by the Constitution (Ninety-seventh Amendment) Act of 2011. It reads as follows:
"43B. Promotion of co-operative societies. - The
State shall endeavour to promote voluntary
formation, autonomous functioning, democratic
control and professional management of co-operative
societies."
5. Undoubtedly, Article 43B, as correctly noted by the learned
Single Judge is a directive principle. It is no doubt true that the
fundamental rights and directive principles can be likened to the
two wheels of a chariot. The directive principles must indeed be
uppermost in the mind of the State and it is to be the guiding
light for the State; but here, the invoking of Article 43B by the

3
writ petitioner appears to be rather farfetched. The writ
petitioner is unable to point out any legal provision apart from
Article 43B, under which he could stake a claim or right to be
allotted 200 acres of land free of cost. The writ petitioner does not
base his claim on any provision, Statute, Rule or Government
Order. We would think that, in such circumstances, the request
to issue a mandamus for the allotment of 200 acres of land and
that too free of cost should not be accepted. The State of
Uttarakhand is predominantly a hilly State. The land, which is
the subject matter of the writ petition, is essentially located in the
plain area. As to what is the best use to which the land is to be
put, is a matter, which is essentially a policy decision and within
the domain of the State.
6. In such circumstances, even proceeding on the basis that
the objective of the writ petitioner is laudable and that
cooperative movement must be encouraged as appears to be the
mandate of Article 43B, we do not think that Article 43B can be
stretched to the extent that it could form the premise of a writ of
mandamus directing 200 acres of land and that too free of cost to
be granted to the writ petitioner.
7. In such circumstances, we agree with the learned Single
Judge and the appeal will stand dismissed without any order as
to cost.
 (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.)
 25.10.2017 25.10.2017
Rahul
